extracted.intended_audience: readers of Nature: practising scientists and scientifically-literate public
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of evaluative criteria and procedural standards embedded in a multi-topic scientific news/notes page (covering chemistry, broadcasting, conferences, meteorology, natural history, etc.). The page is a 1922 issue of Nature containing topical items, obituaries, and short research summaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structural determinants of dye desensitising action
rubrics_metrics.description: “the presence of the characteristic phenazine grouping ... is insufficient in itself, and that amino-groups substituted in the benzene nuclei must also be present.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text reports structure–activity observations for safranines and related dyes: presence of phenazine alone does not confer desensitising power; amino substituents on benzene rings are required. Examples: Neutral Red (a eurhodine) approximates Phenosafranine in desensitising activity; elimination or replacement of amino-groups (e.g. aposafranine, safranones) reduces activity; replacement of both amino-groups by O or OH (safranol) abolishes action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chemical modifications that abolish or reduce desensitising properties
rubrics_metrics.description: “The acetylation of the amino-group, or its diazotisation and copulation with a phenol, destroys the desensitising properties of the safranine, while the replacement by ethyl of the phenyl group attached to the nitrogen has no effect.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance/anti-patterns: modifications such as acetylation or diazotisation (and coupling with a phenol) remove desensitising activity; some substitutions (ethylation of phenyl on N) do not affect activity. These are specific chemical transformations to monitor when assessing or designing desensitisers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical drawback: staining and removal of dyes from gelatin films
rubrics_metrics.description: “The great drawback to the use of Phenosafranine is its pronounced staining properties; it can only be removed from the gelatin film by prolonged washing.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical evaluation criterion for desensitisers: in addition to activity, consider staining/clean-up. Pinakryptol is noted as claimed to be as active as Phenosafranine but without staining gelatin, celluloid, or skin (though it gives a deep green solution), representing a desirable product attribute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hypothesis-testing for mechanism of desensitisation (oxidation product theory)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion of Liippo-Cramer’s claim that desensitising phenomenon is connected with formation of an oxidation product of the dye, countered by Lumière and Seyewetz’s washing/recovery experiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating mechanistic explanations, check empirical tests: unexposed plates bathed in Phenosafranine regain sensitivity after sufficient washing, arguing against irreversible adsorption of an oxidation product on silver bromide. Use experiments that differentiate reversible adsorption from formation of bound oxidation products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broadcasting transmission and programme-quality criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: “It has been found necessary to select carefully the kind of voice which is best suited to the vagaries of the microphone ... simplest sounds, such as in solo pieces, give the best results ... when a number of voices or instruments are operating simultaneously, the microphone is not able to deal faithfully with the various sounds.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance for early wireless broadcasting practice: select performers/voices adapted to microphone characteristics; develop special wireless studio technique and train performers; favour simple/solo items for faithful reproduction; recognize microphone limitations with multiple simultaneous sources; research needed into microphones (or substitutes) that have no prejudice for particular sounds to improve faithfulness of music/speech transmission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conference agenda items as standards for industrial-fuel evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed agenda includes: assay of various fuels; rules for testing boilers, producers, and furnaces; standard methods of making measurements required in controlling the use of fuel; construction of furnaces; use of pulverised fuel and of low-grade fuels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These listed topics serve as a checklist of technical standards and procedural issues for an Industrial Fuel conference — i.e., essential dimensions to standardise when setting industry-wide fuel-testing and utilization guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Daily hemispheric weather-chart scope and content
rubrics_metrics.description: “daily weather charts of the Northern Hemisphere are now being prepared ... The charts ... show barometric pressure and wind for an area covering roughly the temperate zone from the Pacific coast of America in the west to the western borders of Asia in the east.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational standard for meteorological charting: prepare daily, large-area charts for the Northern Hemisphere showing barometric pressure and wind over the temperate zone; display in public/executive locations (e.g. Air Ministry) to aid forecasting. Complement with regional blackboard maps for local detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for published meteorological observations
rubrics_metrics.description: “The observations at Rio de Janeiro are similar in detail to those made at European observatories, hourly values being published of rainfall and sunshine, and detailed monthly results of general meteorological phenomena ... Wind frequency is regularly recorded and also the mean velocity ... tables and maps showing the rainfall ... the various falls being shown in the maps by degrees of shading.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data-publishing standards: use a uniform scale across stations so results are comparable; publish hourly values (e.g. rainfall, sunshine), monthly summaries, wind frequency and mean velocity; include comparisons with long-term means and shaded rainfall maps for halves of year and annual totals. These practices improve utility for aviation and climatology and allow combining provincial results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Information Service response policy
rubrics_metrics.description: “No charge is made for replies to inquiries which do not necessitate a special search for information ... those requests for data which would necessitate the expenditure of a considerable time for accumulation are acknowledged, with an estimate of the cost.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural standard for an information service: provide free answers when an answer can be given from existing assembled files without special searching; for inquiries requiring substantial time/effort, acknowledge receipt and provide a cost estimate. Maintain a staffed team of specialists in contact with current scientific work to service requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal for eugenic testing centres and reporting standard
rubrics_metrics.description: “that eugenists organise centres throughout the country where young persons of eighteen could be given voluntary tests of physical fitness and intelligence, the lists of those who attain standard A being published.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy/procedural criteria: voluntary testing at age eighteen for physical fitness and intelligence; create a published ranking or list (those reaching 'standard A'). This is presented as a mechanism to identify and publicise a national cohort of superior fitness/ability (noting ethical and social implications though the page does not elaborate safeguards).

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental metrics in comparative grass germination studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Reported metrics: percentage of germination (e.g. Poa pratensis 50%, Setaria 95%); time to germination; development of absorbing hairs on coleorhiza and epiblast; depth and spread of roots vs branching; incidence of polyembryony and abnormal types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendations for plant/germination studies: compare species using germination percentage, speed, morphological features (absorbing hairs), root architecture (depth/spread/branching), embryo characteristics (polyembryony), and link abnormalities to possible causes (e.g. insect sting). Include clear plates and bibliographic support for reproducibility.
